sections.html:
The Sampson County Tax Office gathers county, fire district and school district levies, and for now it also collects for Clinton, Autryville, Harrells, Newton Grove, Salemburg, Turkey and Garland. One bill can therefore stack several levies.

Bills for land, buildings and personal property go out by mail in July or August. The state DMV sends the registered vehicle bills. Phone the office at (910) 592-8146 or write to PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329.

Two online tools help: a property record search and a site to search, view and pay bills. Sellers can confirm the parcel, owner and balance there before listing. Print the bill history for your files, since a buyer's agent will usually ask whether the current year is paid. The county's GIS viewer searches by owner name, address or parcel ID and helps you match the tax record to the right lot. That matters when a single address can sit in a town, a fire district and a school district at once.

Payment is due September 1. A 2 percent discount applies to land and personal property paid or postmarked by August 31, and a weekend deadline shifts to the following business day.

  • A bill turns delinquent after January 5, and nothing accrues before then.
  • After that, January adds 2 percent, and each later month adds three-quarters of 1 percent.
  • The office takes partial payments until the delinquency date.
  • A postmark counts as the receipt date for mailed checks.

Parcels still unpaid are advertised in a local newspaper under the owner's name, typically early in April, and the ad cost joins the lien. Collection tools include wage garnishment, bank attachment, seizure and sale, debt setoff and foreclosure.

The county's Tax Rates and Fees page lists these figures under a 2026 heading. Budget years change them, so check with the tax office before relying on any one.

The page also lists some extras. Clinton shows a $25.00 sticker fee, Garland $10.00, Roseboro $9.00, and Newton Grove and Salemburg $5.00 each. Harrells charges $111.00 for trash collection for one and $50.00 for each additional. Fire district rates appear for Plainview, Halls, Coharie, Goshen and Taylors Bridge, and town rates for Harrells, Turkey, Roseboro and Salemburg. Franklin, Turkey and Autryville fire charges apply inside the limits of Harrells, Turkey and Autryville respectively.

Your total depends on which district and town the parcel sits in. Ask the tax office to confirm which ones apply to your address before you quote a figure to a buyer. A bill adds the county-wide rate to the school, fire and municipal figures that apply to it.

Assessed values track market conditions on January 1, 2024, and hold until the next countywide revaluation. The county names 2028 for that, on an eight-year cycle that state law sets (section 105-286).

Market changes after the valuation date cannot lawfully enter an appeal. A sale price well above or below the assessment since 2024 does not by itself move the figure. Facts that existed on the valuation date, such as wrong square footage or a building listed that is gone, make firmer grounds.

Real estate appeals open each January 1 and close when the review board adjourns, typically in early May. An owner told of a changed value only after adjournment has until December 31.

  • Informal review: open to owners whose value moved since the last bill and who are seeing the new figure for the first time. Call (910) 592-8146 or write to Sampson County Tax Department, Attention: Real Estate Appeal, PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329.
  • Formal appeal: phone for a board application. The county commissioners sit as that board, and your application must arrive before adjournment.
  • Next level: the state Property Tax Commission, which needs an application within 30 days of the board mailing its decision.

After you ask for the informal step, an appraiser reviews the parcel again, and you may accept the recommendation or press on to the board. Keep photos or a contractor estimate showing the condition on January 1, 2024 with your request. Write down the date and time of every call, and the name of the person you spoke with, in case you need to follow up.

Personal property appeals run on a 30 day clock from the notice of value. Vehicle appeals need a postmark within 30 days of the notice's printed due date. Vehicles are valued at retail, so supply dealer paperwork and photos in place of web book values.

Three state programs exist, and each owner gets only one. Apply on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office, not in Raleigh. June 1 is the acceptance deadline.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion (section 105-277.1): shields the larger of $25,000 or half of a permanent home's appraised value. The 2026 income ceiling is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion (section 105-277.1C): $45,000 of value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker (section 105-277.1B): caps tax at a percentage of income, 4.0 percent for lower incomes and 5.0 percent for incomes up to 150 percent of the ceiling, and defers the rest.

Deferred circuit breaker tax for the three prior years comes due when the owner transfers the home, dies or stops living in it. A sale triggers it, so get the figure from the tax office before you close. The buyer's title agent will want that amount paid from your proceeds, which lowers what you take home.

Settle the tax through your closing attorney. The county lien attaches on the listing date (section 105-355), so the buyer's title agent will want the year's balance cleared or prorated. Request a payoff for each parcel in the sale from the Sampson County Tax Office.

If the parcel was advertised in April, the ad cost is part of the lien and is owed too. Should a foreclosure follow, the parcel is auctioned at the courthouse door, and a redeeming party pays tax, penalties, interest and costs before confirmation (section 105-374).

After closing, the deed is recorded and the seller owes deed excise tax under section 105-228.30. Buyer and seller can split the year's tax by contract, so write the proration terms down. If you sell before the bill arrives, agree on who pays it and how the figure will be confirmed afterward.

faqs.q: What is the Sampson County payment deadline?
faqs.a: September 1 is the due date. Paying or postmarking by August 31 earns a 2 percent discount, and the account is delinquent after January 5, when 2 percent interest starts for January.

faqs.q: Where can a Sampson County owner contest a real estate value?
faqs.a: Begin with an informal review by phone at (910) 592-8146 if the value changed, or ask for a Board of Equalization and Review application. The cutoff is board adjournment, usually in early May.

faqs.q: When is the next Sampson County revaluation?
faqs.a: In 2028. Until then, assessed values reflect market value on January 1, 2024.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Sampson County tax appeals?
faqs.a: Appeals on real estate and personal property go to the Sampson County Tax Office, PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329, marked with the appeal type. Vehicle appeals may also be emailed to the address on the county's appeal page.

faqs.q: Can a Sampson County homeowner combine a disabled veteran exclusion with another relief program?
faqs.a: No. State law lets an owner benefit from only one of the three programs. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor for the one that fits.
